BearerAuth.description: Pass `Bearer <token>`. JWT is verified by the gateway; the user id arrives as the X-User-Id header.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization

attachment_ids.description:
AttachmentIDs names files uploaded ahead of this turn via
POST /chat/attachments. Each must belong to the caller and, once the
conversation exists, to this thread.

repo_url.description:
RepoURL points a new conversation at a repository, credentials
included. Ignored once the thread exists — a thread works on one
repository, and moving it mid-way would make its own history lie.

timezone.description:
Timezone is the caller's IANA zone (e.g. "Europe/Paris"), used to speak
times in the person's own clock instead of UTC. Empty falls back to UTC.

vote.description: Vote is 1 (up), -1 (down), or 0 to clear a previous vote.

mcp_servers.description:
MCPServers names MCP servers this conversation may use, by name —
never a command. Each name must already be registered on this
deployment (LALTER_MCP_SERVERS), the same registry task uses.

every.description:
Every makes the reminder fire again after this delay instead of once,
read the same way as In ("24h", "7d"). Omitted means one-shot.

Every is the recurrence interval as it was given ("24h"). Absent means
one-shot.

Every, when present, replaces the recurrence: "" clears it back to a
one-shot reminder, anything else sets the new interval.

mcp_servers.description:
MCPServers names MCP servers this run may use, by name — never a
command. Each name must already be registered on this deployment
(LALTER_MCP_SERVERS); an unrecognized name refuses the whole request
with 400 rather than silently running with fewer tools than asked for.

report_diff.description:
ReportDiff asks the run to read back and return the working tree diff
once the agent finishes. A caller giving the agent no write tools has
nothing to read back.

system_prompt.description: SystemPrompt is passed to the agent verbatim.
system_prompt.example: You are diagnosing. Explain what is wrong and why.

tools.description:
Tools names the local tools the agent may use: read, grep, glob, edit,
write, bash. An unrecognized name is silently skipped, not refused.
